description: Saudi immigration officials refused entry to hundreds of Nigerian women pilgrims for not travelling with a husband or male relative. Around 509 would-be pilgrims were affected, some held at the airport for as long as five days. Nigeria suspended pilgrimage flights to Saudi Arabia in response.
energy_note: Five hundred and nine women, refused for arriving alone.

description: She satisfied every Nigerian requirement to depart and every documentary requirement to arrive. The refusal rested on a condition about her companions, which no document could satisfy.
energy_note: Compliant with both countries, and refused by one.

description: Hajj is frequently the single largest discretionary expenditure of a person's life, saved for over years. The refusal did not refund it.
energy_note: A lifetime's saving, spent on five days in an airport.

aspect: The pattern recurs in the labour routes
description: The same principle - that a woman's movement is conditioned on a man's presence or permission - reappears in the Gulf employment contracts in TRF-002, where the permission is the employer's.

aspect: And it is invisible in the aggregate statistics
description: Refusals like this are recorded, if at all, as entry refusals. Nothing in the data says the ground was the absence of a male relative, so the phenomenon does not appear in any dataset of gendered barriers.
energy_note: Counted as a refusal. Not counted as a gendered one.
